articles.title: When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Calibrating expensive engineering simulators requires tuning model parameters to match reference data, a process heavily constrained by computational costs. This study investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs), conditioned on physical diagnostic descriptions of simulation errors, can propose informative parameter updates more efficiently than conventional derivative-free optimizers. articles.title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens du

articles.title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a fact becomes harder to elicit from a language model, has the model lost it, or has it merely become less accessible? Parameter-updating test-time continual learning agents are usually evaluated by current output accuracy; we ask whether that measurement captures how prior experience shapes later updates. We test whether learning a specific factual binding produces a later relearning advantage beyond familiarity with its entity, answer vocabulary, format, or query slot. articles.title: CGDT-CESN: Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network for Multivariate Time-Series Prediction
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.22430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. In this work, a Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network (CGDT-CESN) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series. An innovative reservoir design is proposed in which inter-cluster connections are enabled by empirically observed correlations among variables

articles.title: A single dose of psilocybin eased depression within days, but its edge over placebo faded within a year
articles.summary: A single dose of psilocybin eased depression within days in a small Swedish trial, outperforming an active placebo for more than three months on patients’ self-ratings. By one year, however, the placebo group had largely caught up.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Does medical transition help young transgender people’s mental health? A Finnish study sparks a battle over the answer
articles.summary: A nationwide Finnish study tracked 2,083 young people referred for gender care for as long as 25 years. Specialist psychiatric care rates rose among those who later transitioned medically, though critics dispute what the findings mean.

articles.title: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months linked to fewer ADHD symptoms in children
articles.summary: A large-scale study suggests that infants who exclusively receive breast milk for their first six months may show fewer symptoms of ADHD in early childhood, even when accounting for the child's genetic risks and family socioeconomic background.

articles.title: Genes linked to educational attainment are also tied to fewer behavior problems in kids, mainly through cognitive pathways
articles.summary: Genetic variants linked to how far people go in school are also tied to fewer attention problems and stress-related physical complaints in youth. A study of Dutch families suggests these links run mainly through cognition rather than non-cognitive traits.

articles.title: Brain iron levels in children with ADHD may depend on when they start medication
articles.summary: Children with ADHD who begin taking stimulant medications at a younger age may develop higher brain iron levels than those starting later. A new study explores how treatment timing interacts with brain development in dopamine-rich regions.

articles.title: Intelligence tests are a weaker predictor of job performance than long believed, large study finds
articles.summary: A new synthesis of data from over 109,000 workers suggests that general intelligence tests are less than half as predictive of overall job performance as historical benchmarks claim.

articles.title: Magic mushroom ingredient takes the fight out of aggressive fish
articles.summary: A psychedelic compound found in magic mushrooms appears to have an unexpected effect: calming highly aggressive fish. Researchers discovered that low doses of psilocybin significantly reduced aggressive attacks in mangrove rivulus fish without disrupting their normal social interactions. The findings suggest psilocybin may selectively calm escalating aggression rather than simply suppressing all behavior.

articles.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
articles.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet. Mice given the supplement had lower blood pressure, better memory, and improved social interactions compared with mice consuming excess salt alone.

articles.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
articles.summary: Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months. Researchers also detected changes in gut microbial enzymes, suggesting a possible gut-brain connection, although the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with a placebo.

articles.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression. They also discovered that patients who failed to improve after two years shared a striking pattern: insufficient stimulation of a crucial brain connection. The findings suggest that millimeters in electrode placement could make a major difference in treatment outcomes.
